question:
(a) Explain the variation of photoelectric current with collector potential in a photoelectric experiment.
(b) What is saturation current? Why does the current not increase beyond saturation value?

options.A:
(a) Current is maximum at zero collector potential and becomes zero for positive potential.
(b) Saturation current occurs when the metal stops emitting electrons.
options.B:
(a) Current is independent of collector potential.
(b) Saturation current is reached when photon energy becomes zero.
options.C:
(a) Negative collector potential attracts more electrons.
(b) Current increases indefinitely after saturation.
options.D:
(a) Positive collector potential attracts more photoelectrons, so current rises; negative potential repels them, so current falls.
(b) Saturation current is the maximum current when all emitted photoelectrons are collected. Beyond this, collector potential cannot increase the number of electrons emitted per second, so the current remains constant.
